seed: A circle with a border, and a line. The border is saved as a style from the Border section's own Style row, which is what 'the style of the circle border' means. The line's Color menu then has to offer that colour: not as a name to follow, because a line cannot follow a border, but as a colour to paint with, saying where it came from. Reported by the user on 2026-09-15: 'any style which holds a color should be usable for a color style'.

steps.note: a circle wearing one border, in a colour of its own
THE MOVE THE USER MADE: the border saved under a name. It is a saved EFFECT, not a saved COLOUR, and before this change the colour in it had no way out of the style.

THE TEST: the line's Color row. borrowedColors must read ['Circle edge (border)'] — the colour inside the saved border, offered on a line, saying where it came from. styles must still be empty, because the border is not a colour the line can WEAR.

the line is now the colour the circle's border is, in one pick. selectedColors must show the line's colour with no style name on it: the colour landed and the name stayed behind, which is the same answer a drag of a colour kept for other parts gives.

ONE undo puts the line back. Undo is asked for as a menu action rather than as command Z, because a synthesized chord does not reach the Edit menu of an app that is not in front (see undo-shortcut-walk).
